item.title: Complete reducibility of integrable quantum modules with bounded weights and finite-dimensional weight spaces
item.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module such that (a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every $\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]); (b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$; and (c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every $i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$; concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some $\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used exactly to select bases of the set-indexed family of finite-dimensional maximal-vector spaces simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-submodule, the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is choice-free. The finite-cone modules use explicit label grading and the regularization supplier when the original pairing is not separating.
item.strategy: Choose one finite-support regularization for the upper cones; it preserves the grading, all E/F actions and reconstructs the old torus, so prove the statement in the regular support category and transport back. For any vector, U^{≥0}v has finitely many weights: the upper set of each of its finitely many support labels inside the finite union of cones is finite, and each weight has finite dimension. An integrable cyclic highest submodule is the simple L(lambda) by the completed early universality theorem. For restricted duality use the Q(q)-linear anti-involution phi fixing the torus and interchanging E_i,F_i (tau composed with bar), on M^*=⊕_mu Hom(M_mu,Q(q)). Finite-dimensional weights give M=M^{**}. To verify integrability of the dual, each rank-one cyclic submodule in M is finite dimensional: commute its E/F powers into F^bE^a form, and use local nilpotence on the finitely many E^a v. The generic rank-one finite modules split into finite simple strings by their distinct Casimir scalars, with equal highest labels split by the top-vector bases. The finite sum U_iM_mu therefore captures every string contributing to the mu-coordinate and gives a uniform exponent for the transpose arrows into that coordinate; the dual is integrable. Fix a globally maximal weight lambda in a nonzero submodule, a vector v_lambda, and extend its evaluation functional to the full finite-dimensional M_lambda with value1 on v_lambda. This gives phi_lambda∈M^*_lambda (not merely a functional on V). Since no higher label exists, it is highest. Its cyclic W is L(lambda). Dualizing W→M^* gives M→W^*; its restriction to V=U_qv_lambda is nonzero on the top and hence an isomorphism between the simple highest modules. Invert that restriction to obtain a retraction M→V and split. If M=U_qF for finite-dimensional U^{≥0}-stable F, choose a maximal weight of F: it is globally maximal in M because multiplying negative words only lowers the finite weights of F. The retraction reduces the dimension of the generating image of F, giving finite induction. For arbitrary M every cyclic submodule is of that form, so M is a sum of simple submodules. Under AC select a maximal independent family of them (Zorn, or simultaneous singular bases) and prove it spans: a simple submodule not contained in the sum intersects it either in itself or zero, and the latter would enlarge the family. This yields the algebraic direct sum. The normalized sigma-form gives the equivalent self-dual identification; no nonexistent extension from V^* to M^* is asserted without explicitly choosing the functional in M_lambda.

references.title: Kyeonghoon Jeong, Seok-Jin Kang and Masaki Kashiwara, Crystal Bases for Quantum Generalized Kac-Moody Algebras, arXiv:math/0305390
references.locator: §3, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.7, printed pp. 10-13: the category $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the finite dual $M^*$ and Lemma 3.5, the splitting Lemma 3.6 (a highest weight submodule generated by a maximal vector is a direct summand), and the complete reducibility Theorem 3.7; Corollary 3.8 (direct sums of finite-dimensional $U_i$-submodules).

references.title: Richard Borcherds, Mark Haiman, Theo Johnson-Freyd, Nicolai Reshetikhin and Vera Serganova, Berkeley Lectures on Lie Groups and Quantum Groups (book-length lecture notes, last updated 18 January 2024)
references.locator: Ch. 13, §13.2.1, Corollary 13.2.1.11, printed p. 318: semisimplicity of the finite-dimensional part of the category for transcendental $q$, proved by splitting an extension using the highest weight vector and the dual.

references.title: George Lusztig, Introduction to Quantum Groups (Progress in Mathematics 110, Birkhauser, 1993; second printing 1994; author-hosted scan)
references.locator: Ch. 3, §3.5 and Ch. 6, §6.2: complete reducibility of integrable highest weight modules and their contravariant duality.

item.axiom_use: AC is used only for the simultaneous selection of bases in the set-indexed family of finite-dimensional maximal-vector (singular) weight spaces and for the resulting algebraic direct-sum decomposition over an arbitrary index set, as in the classical analogue; the splitting lemma, the finite-induction case of modules generated by one finite-dimensional $U^{\ge0}$-submodule, and all integrability computations are choice-free.

comparison.confirmed_counterexample: In sl3 L(Lambda2), highest h1 integer0; F2v is nonzero and has h1 integer1 because a12=-1. Upper Q+ cone support does not bound every h_i value by the upper-label h_i integers.
comparison.smallest_sound_route: Restore rank-one finite-string control. The proposed local proof bounds each fixed alpha_i line through a label by finite upper-cone coefficients and finite string endpoints, so restricted duals are locally nilpotent without any global coroot bound.

comparison.confirmed_counterexample: F the two top lines of L(Lambda1) directsum L(Lambda2) has two incomparable maximal labels; neither dominates the other
comparison.smallest_sound_route: Keep finite-union support; maximality of mu rules out N_(mu+alpha_i) and proves N_mu=F_mu without comparing all other labels to mu. Use a finite graded hull and the finite-simple-sum argument for ordinary ungraded submodules.
